sentences.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption repeated its employee survey in 1999 to assess how NSW public sector perceptions and reporting attitudes had changed since 1993.
sentences.support:
In 1999, the Independent Commission Against Corruption repeated its 1993 Unravelling 
Corruption survey

sentences.text: The research compared responses to workplace scenarios and examined whether experience in particular work affected recognition of corruption and willingness to act.

sentences.text: ICAC concluded that respondents more often recognised corruption and said they would report it, while unclear definitions and fear of retaliation remained barriers.

sentences.text: ICAC set out six main lessons about shared understanding, selection-panel training, reporting channels, induction, management action and creating a safe reporting culture.
sentences.support:
More needs to be done to create organisational cultures in which employees feel 
safe to report corruption.
sentences.section: Major lessons for corruption minimisation in the public sector

findings.quote:
More needs to be done to create organisational cultures in which employees feel 
safe to report corruption.

Review the nature of training given to those who participate in selection panels to 
address the risks identified in recruitment selection.

notes: The six numbered items are labelled major lessons, not formal numbered recommendations. Survey scenarios and attitudes are not findings of actual misconduct.
